flags: Management and the independent auditor concluded that substantial doubt existed about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern due to debt obligations, historical negative cash flows, and recurring losses.

loss_record.explanation: AVITA Medical has incurred operating losses since inception because its operating expenses—primarily sales and marketing, general and administrative, and research and development—have consistently exceeded gross profit. Operating losses continued through 2023–2025 and the first nine months of 2026.

quotes.quote: The Company has incurred operating losses and negative cash flows from operations since its inception and has an accumulated deficit of $432.9 million as of September 30, 2026.
We anticipate that we may continue to incur losses at least until sales of our products are adequate to fund operating expenses.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P1 and P5
business_model.claim: AVITA Medical commercializes an acute wound care portfolio comprising RECELL (including RECELL EOU, RECELL GO, and RECELL GO mini), Cohealyx, and PermeaDerm.
quotes: Our current commercial portfolio includes RECELL® (“RECELL”), and two complementary wound care products, PermeaDerm® and Cohealyx™, which together support a comprehensive standard of care for acute wounds.
The single-use RECELL Autologous Cell Harvesting Device (“RECELL Ease-of-Use” or “RECELL EOU”) is approved by the FDA for the treatment of thermal burn wounds and full-thickness skin defects.
Our next-generation device, RECELL GO® Autologous Cell Harvesting Device (“RECELL GO”), is FDA-approved to treat thermal burn wounds and full-thickness skin defects.

RECELL GO mini® Autologous Cell Harvesting Device (“RECELL GO mini”), which was approved by the FDA in December 2024, is a line extension of RECELL GO, designed specifically to treat smaller wounds up to 480 cm2.

business_model.basis: stated directly in F2, P1, and P3
business_model.claim: RECELL generates revenue from single-use cell harvesting devices and preparation kits (RPKs) used with a multi-use processing device (RPD), and the company records both sales revenue and lease revenue.
quotes: RECELL is an autologous cell harvesting technology that enables clinicians to create a suspension of a patient’s own skin cells, called Spray-On Skin™, at the point of care.
It consists of two components: the RECELL GO Processing Device (the “RPD”) and the RECELL GO Preparation Kit (the “RPK”).
The RPD is a multi-use, AC-powered device that controls the RPK.
The RPK contains a single-use cartridge and the RECELL Enzyme™.
Lease revenue | 252 | 165 | 652 | 547

business_model.basis: stated directly in P5 and P8
business_model.claim: RECELL is the primary revenue driver, generating $22.4 million in U.S. revenue in the third quarter of 2026 alongside $2.1 million from Cohealyx, $0.6 million from PermeaDerm, and $0.9 million from international sales out of approximately $26.1 million in total revenue.
quotes: Total revenue was approximately $26.1 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 53% compared to $17.1 million in the prior-year period.
RECELL (Q3 U.S. revenue of $22.4 million, approximately 20% growth compared to Q2 2026) continued to drive the business, reflecting higher procedure volumes and increased account ordering.

Cohealyx (Q3 revenue of $2.1 million, approximately 21% growth compared to Q2 2026) continued to build commercial momentum, reflecting an expanding customer base and additional hospital value analysis committee (VAC) approvals.
PermeaDerm (Q3 revenue of $0.6 million, essentially flat compared to Q2 2026) maintained stable revenue.
International (Q3 revenue of $0.9 million, essentially flat compared to Q2 2026) continued to contribute consistent revenue from established international markets.
Cohealyx and PermeaDerm represented 8% and 2%, respectively, of total commercial sales.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P1 and P5
business_model.claim: In the U.S., the company focuses on approximately 200 burn and trauma centers as well as surgical settings treating thermal burns and full-thickness skin defects, while pausing further commercial investment in vitiligo due to limited and uncertain reimbursement.
quotes: We are executing a focused commercial strategy centered on approximately 200 U.S. burn and trauma centers that represent the highest value and procedural volume within the acute wound care market.

With the expansion of RECELL indications to include full-thickness skin defects, we have broadened our commercial focus to additional trauma and surgical settings that treat complex acute wounds and often share clinical, operational, and economic characteristics with burn centers.
Despite regulatory approval and demonstrated clinical benefit, reimbursement for vitiligo procedures remains limited and uncertain.
As a result, we have paused further commercial investment in vitiligo at this time.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P2, P5, and P8
business_model.claim: Outside the U.S., AVITA Medical sells through third-party distributors in approved markets—including Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Japan—and also holds a ten-year BARDA agreement worth up to $25.5 million for mass-casualty RECELL supply and readiness services.
quotes: We rely on third-party distributors for a portion of our sales in countries outside of the U.S.
RECELL and RECELL GO® are CE-marked in Europe, have TGA certification in Australia, and are listed with Medsafe in New Zealand; RECELL is PMDA-approved in Japan.

On April 6, 2026, we entered into a ten-year agreement with the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (“BARDA”), part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, with a total potential value of up to $25.5 million.
Under the agreement, we will maintain a supply of RECELL for deployment in mass casualty incidents and provide associated readiness and support services.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P5 and P11
business_model.claim: The company markets and distributes Cohealyx exclusively in the U.S. under an agreement with manufacturer Regenity Biosciences, and manufactures and distributes PermeaDerm in the U.S. under exclusive agreements with Stedical Scientific, which may also buy PermeaDerm from AVITA for unserved U.S. and non-U.S. markets.
quotes: Regenity manufactures and supplies Cohealyx™, an AVITA Medical-branded, FDA-cleared, collagen-based dermal matrix.

Under the agreement with Regenity, we hold the exclusive rights to market, sell, and distribute Cohealyx in the U.S., with the potential to expand such commercialization into the European Union, Australia, and Japan.

In addition, in the United States, we hold the rights to manufacture and exclusively market, sell, and distribute PermeaDerm®, a biosynthetic wound matrix, under the terms of exclusive multi-year distribution and contract manufacturing agreements with Stedical Scientific, Inc.
Also under the Global Amendment, Stedical may pursue the commercialization of PermeaDerm in certain U.S. markets not currently served by the Company.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P3 and P5
business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by deeper penetration in existing customer accounts, new accounts treating traumatic and surgical wounds, adoption of RECELL GO mini for smaller wounds, and hospital Value Analysis Committee (VAC) approvals for Cohealyx.
quotes: The growth in revenues was largely driven by deeper penetration within customer accounts, new accounts for the treatment of traumatic and surgical wounds and, to a lesser extent, new product launches.

The increase in RECELL sales was due to continued normalization in RECELL utilization following the publication by all of the MACs of reimbursement rates related to healthcare providers use of RECELL and also higher sales of RECELL GO mini in trauma and smaller wounds.
Cohealyx sales increased 154%, or $1.3 million, primarily driven by more Value Analysis Committees (“VAC”) approvals allowing broader adoption of the product in more facilities.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P3, P5, and P8
business_model.claim: Third-party reimbursement directly moves RECELL demand: regional MAC pricing delays in 2025 slowed utilization until all seven MACs published rates by March 2026, while CMS approved an inpatient NTAP of up to $4,875 per case and finalized national physician payment values effective in 2027.
quotes: Delay by the MACs in establishing and publishing reimbursement rates temporarily slowed clinician use of RECELL.
As of March 2026, all seven MACs had published rates, restoring reimbursement clarity and supporting a return toward normalized utilization.

This NTAP designation allows Medicare Part A inpatient claims to receive up to $4,875 in additional reimbursement per case, beyond the standard MS-DRG base rate, provided CMS thresholds and coding criteria are met.
On November 4, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services finalized national physician payment values and simplified billing codes for RECELL procedures, effective January 1, 2027

business_model.basis: stated directly in P3, P5, P8, and P11
business_model.claim: Revenue-sharing on Cohealyx and PermeaDerm lowers consolidated gross margin (82.1% in 2025 and 84.0% in the third quarter of 2026) relative to standalone RECELL gross margin (84.3% in 2025 and 88.4% in the third quarter of 2026), although an August 2026 amendment raised AVITA's PermeaDerm revenue share to 67% for sheets and 80% for gloves.
quotes: Gross profit margin was 82.1% compared to 85.8% in the corresponding period in the prior year.
Note that the gross margin for RECELL products only was 84.3% for the year.
Note that the gross margin for RECELL products on a standalone basis was 88.4% for the quarter.
Gross margin was 84.0%, an increase of 270 basis points year over year, reflecting higher RECELL revenue and improvements in manufacturing efficiency
The Company receives 50% of the average sales price for Cohealyx and up to 55% for PermeaDerm, which lowers the overall gross margin percentage.

In addition, the Company’s share of revenue from PermeaDerm sales will increase to 67% for products sold in sheet form, subject to increased revenue sharing in the event the Company’s gross margin on those products exceeds 50%, and to 80% for products sold in glove form, subject to increased revenue sharing in the event the Company’s gross margin on those products exceeds 35%.

business_model.basis: stated directly in P2, P3, and P8
business_model.claim: On the supply and production side, AVITA Medical manufactures, packages, and warehouses RECELL and PermeaDerm at its Ventura, California facility while relying on third-party and some single-source suppliers for RECELL components, with gross margin affected by product mix, manufacturing efficiency, and inventory reserves.
quotes: We have a manufacturing facility located in Ventura, California where we produce, package, and warehouse RECELL and PermeaDerm.
We also rely on global third-party manufacturers for production of some of the components used in RECELL.
Due to the cost and regulatory requirements associated with qualifying multiple suppliers, in 2023, we single-sourced some of our material components.
The decrease in the overall gross margin percentage from the prior year was primarily caused by product mix and higher inventory reserve.

quotes: Total operating expenses decreased by 9% or $10.4 million to $101.4 million, compared with $111.8 million in the year-ended December 31, 2024.
Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 9%, or $5.1 million, to $53.1 million, compared to $58.2 million in the year-ended December 31, 2024.
General and administrative expenses decreased by 18%, or $5.8 million, to $27.3 million, compared to $33.1 million in the year-ended December 31, 2024.
Research and development expenses increased by 2%, or $0.5 million, to $20.8 million, compared to $20.3 million in the year-ended December 31, 2024.
The increase was driven largely by higher sales and marketing expenses, which rose $1.5 million due primarily to increased commissions and compensation, including annual incentive costs.

competitive_position.claim: AVITA Medical centers its acute wound care portfolio on RECELL, an FDA-approved autologous cell harvesting device, alongside exclusive U.S. rights to Cohealyx and PermeaDerm.
quotes: At the forefront of our portfolio is RECELL® (“RECELL”), approved by the United States Food & Drug Administration (the “FDA”) for the treatment of thermal burn wounds and full-thickness skin defects.

Under the agreement with Regenity, we hold the exclusive rights to market, sell, and distribute Cohealyx in the U.S., with the potential to expand such commercialization into the European Union, Australia, and Japan.

quotes: The U.S. burn treatment market is highly concentrated, with approximately 140 specialized burn centers treating the majority of severe burn patients.
We are executing a focused commercial strategy centered on approximately 200 U.S. burn and trauma centers that represent the highest value and procedural volume within the acute wound care market.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1 Business)
competitive_position.claim: Expansion into full-thickness skin defects gives RECELL an estimated addressable market of approximately 272,000 U.S. procedures annually across trauma, surgical wounds, and cancer resections.
quotes: In the U.S., we estimate that approximately 272,000 procedures annually may be eligible for treatment with RECELL across traumatic injuries, surgical wounds, and cancer-related resections.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1 Business)
competitive_position.claim: Pivotal trials and retrospective studies show RECELL reduced donor-skin requirements by up to 97.5% for second-degree burns and 32% for third-degree burns, and reduced mean autograft procedures by 56% in pediatric cases and 60% in adults over 50% TBSA.
quotes: In pivotal clinical trials, RECELL significantly reduced donor-skin requirements by up to 97.5% for second-degree burns and 32% for third-degree burns when used with meshed autografts, compared to standard of care autografting, without compromising healing.
In pediatric cases (N = 284), treatment with RECELL resulted in a 56% reduction in the mean number of autograft procedures required compared to National Burn Registry (“NBR”) data.
Additionally, in adult patients with greater than 50% TBSA (N=318), RECELL resulted in a 60% reduction in the mean number of autograft procedures versus NBR data.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 7 MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: Real-world registry data from 741 matched adult patients showed RECELL was associated with a 36% reduction in hospital length of stay, and a systematic review of 99 peer-reviewed studies supported its clinical and economic benefits.
quotes: A registry-based analysis of 741 matched adult patients with deep partial-thickness burns from the American Burn Association’s Burn Care Quality Platform compared RECELL with split-thickness skin grafting.

The study demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in hospital length of stay of approximately 5.6 days, or 36%, for RECELL-treated patients, with consistent reductions across burn size subgroups up to 30% TBSA.

A systematic review of 99 peer-reviewed studies, including 27 comparative analyses and more than 8,000 patients, found that RECELL consistently reduced donor site burden, achieved healing times comparable to or faster than conventional grafting, and demonstrated favorable pain, aesthetic and health economic outcomes across wound types.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-Q Item 2 MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: Post-market studies showed Cohealyx reduced mean time to autografting readiness to 13.6 days versus 33.2 days for a literature benchmark, while PermeaDerm achieved 70% lower product cost and 95.7% less preparation time than allograft.
quotes: In April 2026, we announced positive interim results from our Cohealyx I post-market clinical study, demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in mean time to autografting readiness of approximately 20 days compared to a literature-derived benchmark (13.6 days versus 33.2 days; p<0.001).

The study met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a 70% lower mean product cost per 1% total body surface area treated with PermeaDerm (p<0.001), and showed a 95.7% reduction in preparation time, comparable graft take and wound healing, and no adverse events attributed to PermeaDerm.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: The company faces intense competition from rivals with significantly greater financial and development resources who could introduce products that make AVITA Medical's offerings obsolete.
quotes: The markets for our products are highly competitive and our competitors may develop products that may more effectively compete with our products.
Our competitors may have significantly more financial and other resources to invest in product development.

We must, therefore, continue to develop and market new products, or we risk our products becoming obsolete, in which case, our revenues may decline, adversely impacting our financial condition or our business prospects.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
